_meta.description: Stylistic archetypes per position with verified academy bios sourced from public biographical data (Wikipedia, Transfermarkt, FBref, club academy pages, long-form journalism). Each archetype includes signature_attrs (must-have score gates), anchor (weighted attrs for the style lens), profile (foot/build/role/path — used by the build, role and path lenses), and academy_bio (age-bracketed biographical facts used for age-aware comparisons). NEVER publishes numeric youth scores for any named professional — only sourced biographical facts.

attacking midfielder.name: Modric-type composer
attacking midfielder.summary: Composed playmaker who controls tempo with scanning and elite ball-handling.

academy_bio.8-10: Started in NK Zadar's youth section around age 6, growing up in Croatia during the war. Always the smallest in his age group but already known locally for not losing the ball.
academy_bio.11-12: Around U12 was tried at Hajduk Split (Croatia's biggest academy) — rejected for being 'too thin and small to make it'. Returned to NK Zadar and kept playing weekly.
academy_bio.13-14: U13-U14 at NK Zadar — small playmaker, dropped deep to receive because he wasn't tall enough to win duels higher up. Caught Dinamo Zagreb scouts' attention at youth tournaments.
academy_bio.15-17: Signed by Dinamo Zagreb academy at 16. Senior first-team debut at 17 — composure under pressure was already first-team quality before the legs caught up.
academy_bio.18-21: Loaned to Zrinjski Mostar (Bosnian league) at 18 to toughen up physically. Returned to Dinamo at 19 as a regular. Tottenham at 22, Real Madrid at 26.

attacking midfielder.name: Ödegaard-type composer
attacking midfielder.summary: Arsenal's brain — composes the side with elite scanning and weight.

academy_bio.8-10: Joined Strømsgodset (Drammen, Norway) youth around age 7. Father Hans Erik was a Norwegian pro, so football was the family rhythm from very young.
academy_bio.11-12: U12 at Strømsgodset — already known in Norwegian junior football for picking out a pass other kids couldn't see. Skipped most U13 youth football to train with older boys.
academy_bio.13-14: U13-U14 at Strømsgodset — training regularly with U16 and U18 squads. Norwegian FA flagged him as the most talented academy product in a generation.
academy_bio.15-17: Senior Strømsgodset debut at 15 — became the youngest player in Tippeligaen history. Sold to Real Madrid at 16 for ~€3m. Spent 16-21 on loan tours (Heerenveen, Vitesse, Real Sociedad, Arsenal).
academy_bio.18-21: Loan years at Heerenveen, Vitesse and Real Sociedad shaped the modern Ödegaard — added composure under physical pressure. Permanent Arsenal move at 22, captain by 23.

attacking midfielder.name: Pedri-type press-breaker
attacking midfielder.summary: Press-resistant micro-genius — escapes pressure to find the next pass.

academy_bio.8-10: Started in Tegueste (small village in Tenerife, Canary Islands) around age 6 at the local club Juventud Laguna — playing barefoot in family yards before that.
academy_bio.11-12: Joined CD Tegueste U12 — already a head shorter than his teammates but rarely lost the ball in tight space.
academy_bio.13-14: Joined UD Las Palmas (Canary Islands pro club) academy at 14. Coaches said he was the only kid who 'played with his head up since the day he arrived'.
academy_bio.15-17: Las Palmas first team at 16 (Segunda División). Sold to Barcelona at 17 for ~€5m. Many big clubs (including Real Madrid) had watched him at 14-15 but didn't sign him because of his frame.
academy_bio.18-21: Barcelona first-team debut at 17. Started for Spain at the Euros at 18. Euro 2020 Young Player of the Tournament. Has battled hamstring issues from playing too many minutes too young.

attacking midfielder.name: De Bruyne-type chance creator
attacking midfielder.summary: Chance-creating machine — playing as a #10 his vision becomes lethal.

academy_bio.8-10: Joined KVV Drongen youth (small Belgian club) at age 6. Moved to Gent at 9-10 — known locally for hitting passes other kids his age couldn't even attempt.
academy_bio.11-12: Joined Genk academy at 11 — Genk being the top Belgian academy at the time alongside Anderlecht.
academy_bio.13-14: U13-U14 at Genk — was already striking the ball with the technique of a senior. Lived in academy housing during the week.
academy_bio.15-17: Genk youth → first-team debut at 17 (Belgian Pro League). Sold to Chelsea at 21 — never broke through, sent on loan to Werder Bremen.
academy_bio.18-21: Werder Bremen loan transformed him. Sold to Wolfsburg at 22, Bundesliga player of the season at 23. Manchester City at 24.

attacking midfielder.name: Bruno Fernandes-type chaos
attacking midfielder.summary: High-risk high-reward chaos creator — every action could be the killer ball.

academy_bio.8-10: Joined Boavista (Porto, Portugal) youth at age 8. Played up two age groups consistently because he was bigger physically.
academy_bio.11-12: U12 at Boavista — already showing the volume-shooting habit. Would attempt long-range shots multiple times a game even at U12.
academy_bio.13-14: U13-U14 at Boavista's academy — relentless work rate flagged by coaches. Wasn't flashy technically but always influenced games.
academy_bio.15-17: Moved to Italy at 17 (Novara, Serie B) on a youth contract — unusually direct route, bypassing the Portuguese senior academy.
academy_bio.18-21: Udinese at 18 (Serie A). Sampdoria at 22. Back to Portugal (Sporting CP) at 22 — became Portugal's player of the year before joining Manchester United at 25.

attacking midfielder.name: Bellingham-type complete 8
attacking midfielder.summary: Generational midfielder — arrives in the box, defends, leads, scores.

academy_bio.8-10: Joined Birmingham City academy at 7 — local boy, his dad and brother both played for nearby teams.
academy_bio.11-12: U12 at Birmingham — already a head taller than peers and physically dominant. Captained his age group from U11 onwards.
academy_bio.13-14: U13-U14 at Birmingham — training regularly with the U18s. Birmingham retired his shirt number when he left — first English club to do so for an academy product.
academy_bio.15-17: Birmingham senior debut at 16 (Championship). Captained Birmingham at 17. Sold to Borussia Dortmund at 17 for £25m — record fee for an English 17-year-old.
academy_bio.18-21: Bundesliga player of the year-equivalent at 18. Real Madrid at 19 for £100m+. Champions League and La Liga winner at 20.

attacking midfielder.name: Foden-type inverted
attacking midfielder.summary: Plays multiple roles around the #10 with elite ball-carrying and finish.

academy_bio.8-10: Joined Manchester City academy at age 8. Local Stockport boy who would walk to Etihad Campus from a young age.
academy_bio.11-12: U12 at Man City — already drawing comparisons to David Silva in the academy. Coaches said his close control at 11 was 'unlike anyone we'd ever had'.
academy_bio.13-14: U13-U14 at City — winning every academy player of the year award. Trained with first team occasionally even at 14.
academy_bio.15-17: U18 captain at 16. Senior debut at 17 in the EFL Cup. England U17 World Cup-winning captain at 17 — best player at the tournament.
academy_bio.18-21: First Premier League start at 18. Champions League appearances at 19. By 21, established starter at Manchester City.

attacking midfielder.name: Jamal Musiala-type dribbler
attacking midfielder.summary: Carries the ball through any defence with feet too quick to follow.

academy_bio.8-10: Born in Germany, moved to England at 7. Joined Southampton youth at 8 — chosen over local Hampshire kids because of his close control.
academy_bio.11-12: Chelsea academy from 11. Lived in the Cobham academy housing — already standing out in the elite English youth setup.
academy_bio.13-14: U13-U14 at Chelsea — frequently played up two age groups. Eligible for England, Germany and Nigeria — England capped him first.
academy_bio.15-17: Surprise move to Bayern Munich at 16 — Chelsea couldn't guarantee a first-team pathway. Bayern senior debut at 17. Switched international allegiance to Germany at 18.
academy_bio.18-21: Bundesliga and Champions League regular by 19. Top scorer in the Bundesliga at 20. Considered the heir to Germany's #10 spot.

attacking midfielder.name: Lamine Yamal-type wonderkid
attacking midfielder.summary: Generational wonderkid — beats players and creates in equal measure.

academy_bio.8-10: Joined Barcelona's La Masia at age 7 — local Catalan kid (Mataró), spotted in a school competition.
academy_bio.11-12: U12 at La Masia — Xavi (then U10/U12 coach) reportedly told staff 'this one is different' when Yamal was 11.
academy_bio.13-14: U13-U14 La Masia — training with the older youth teams. La Liga staff already monitoring him for the senior squad pathway.
academy_bio.15-17: Barcelona B at 14. First-team debut at 15 years, 290 days — youngest in Barcelona history. Played at Euro 2024 at 16, becoming youngest goalscorer in tournament history.
academy_bio.18-21: Established starter for Barcelona at 16-17. Already in Ballon d'Or conversations at 17 — comparisons with the all-time greats are running ahead of his actual career.

attacking midfielder.name: Olise-type creator
attacking midfielder.summary: Left-foot magician — creates from wide #10 zones with elegant delivery.

academy_bio.8-10: Joined Chelsea academy at 8 — born in London to a French-Nigerian-Algerian family, multilingual upbringing.
academy_bio.11-12: U12 at Chelsea — already showing the left-foot delivery range that would define him later.
academy_bio.13-14: Released by Chelsea at U14 — deemed not athletic enough for the elite English pathway. Picked up by Reading academy.
academy_bio.15-17: Reading U18s. Senior debut at 16-17 in the Championship. Played in unfashionable lower-tier English football for several seasons.
academy_bio.18-21: Sold to Crystal Palace at 19 for ~£8m — Premier League breakthrough. Sold to Bayern Munich at 22 for ~€60m. A true 'rejected then redemption' story.

attacking midfielder.name: Kobbie Mainoo-type emerging 8
attacking midfielder.summary: Young academy prodigy with the composure of a senior midfielder.

academy_bio.8-10: Joined Manchester United academy at 9 — local Stockport boy (same area as Phil Foden).
academy_bio.11-12: U12 at United — already drawing comparisons within the academy for ball-retention under pressure.
academy_bio.13-14: U13-U14 at United — training regularly with the U18s.
academy_bio.15-17: United U18 captain at 17. Senior debut at 18 — Erik ten Hag fast-tracked him into the first team. FA Cup goal in the final at 18.
academy_bio.18-21: England senior debut at 18. Established Manchester United starter by 19 — quickest English academy product to break through in a decade.

attacking midfielder.name: Mahrez-type late breakthrough
attacking midfielder.summary: Late-blooming breakthrough — proves that not every elite career starts in elite academies.

academy_bio.8-10: Born in Paris suburbs (Sarcelles) — played street football through his pre-teen years. Never in a top French academy at this age.
academy_bio.11-12: Played for AAS Sarcelles (regional amateur club) — completely off the elite academy radar.
academy_bio.13-14: Still at AAS Sarcelles U14-U16 — slim build, no big-club interest. Family situation meant football was a hobby, not a project.
academy_bio.15-17: Late move to Quimper (Ligue 2 reserves) at ~18. Played in lower-tier French football — Le Havre B-side at 21. Still no Premier League radar.
academy_bio.18-21: Le Havre senior team. Leicester City scouted him at 23 in Ligue 2. Premier League title winner at 24-25. PFA Player of the Year same season. Manchester City for £60m at 27. Proves elite ceiling is achievable from semi-pro starts.

attacking midfielder.name: Florian Wirtz-type creator
attacking midfielder.summary: Creative engine — beats his man and finds the killer ball in the same motion.

academy_bio.8-10: Joined Köln youth at 7 — Pulheim local boy, near the Köln training ground.
academy_bio.11-12: U12 at Köln — known as one of the most technically advanced kids in the German youth pyramid.
academy_bio.13-14: U13-U14 at Köln academy — by U14 was widely regarded as the best youth prospect in Germany.
academy_bio.15-17: Surprise move to Bayer Leverkusen at 16 (Köln couldn't guarantee fast-track). Senior debut at 17. Bundesliga regular by 17-18.
academy_bio.18-21: ACL injury at 19 — recovered fully. Bundesliga title winner at 20 (Leverkusen's first ever). Real Madrid and Bayern interest at 21-22.

goalkeeper.name: Manuel Neuer-type sweeper
goalkeeper.summary: Plays the highest line in the league — sweeps behind the defence and starts attacks at his feet.

goalkeeper.name: Alisson-type modern keeper
goalkeeper.summary: Composure-first keeper who turns saves into counter-attacks within two passes.

goalkeeper.name: Courtois-type shot-stopper
goalkeeper.summary: Old-school commanding keeper whose size and timing make every save look routine.

goalkeeper.name: Ter Stegen-type passer
goalkeeper.summary: Treats build-up like a midfielder — both-footed range opens up the press.

goalkeeper.name: Mike Maignan-type athlete
goalkeeper.summary: Athletic shot-stopper who turns recoveries into impossible saves with raw pace.

goalkeeper.name: Donnarumma-type reflex
goalkeeper.summary: Tall, springy keeper whose reflexes win the moments others can't even reach.

goalkeeper.name: David Raya-type distributor
goalkeeper.summary: Conducts the back four with both feet and intelligent claiming on crosses.

goalkeeper.name: Jan Oblak-type positional
goalkeeper.summary: Saves through angles, not athleticism — the cleanest positional keeper in Europe.

goalkeeper.name: Ederson-type playmaker
goalkeeper.summary: Plays like an extra deep-lying playmaker — pinpoint long range from his own box.

centre back.name: Van Dijk-type leader
centre back.summary: Defends with brain and presence first — the modern complete leader CB.

centre back.name: Rüdiger-type enforcer
centre back.summary: Plays on the front foot — closes ground in two steps and wins every duel he enters.

centre back.name: Bastoni-type ball-player
centre back.summary: A Serie A modern CB who builds attacks like a deep-lying midfielder.

centre back.name: Saliba-type complete CB
centre back.summary: The blueprint for the modern CB — pace, positioning and elite ball-playing.

centre back.name: Kim Min-jae-type aggressor
centre back.summary: Asian CB who proves the modern game needs aerobic CBs — duels, sprints, repeats.

centre back.name: Araújo-type athletic CB
centre back.summary: Defends a high line confidently because his recovery pace covers most threats.

centre back.name: Stones-type inverted CB
centre back.summary: Inverts into midfield mid-possession — redefines what CB technicality means.

centre back.name: Marquinhos-type reader
centre back.summary: Defends with the brain — reads the game two moves ahead, leads the line vocally.

centre back.name: Konaté-type powerful CB
centre back.summary: Physical specimen who combines pace and power — wins every duel, recovers any ball.

full back.name: Trent Alexander-Arnold-type
full back.summary: Plays full-back like a deep-lying playmaker — creates more chances than most #10s.

full back.name: João Cancelo-type inverted
full back.summary: Inverts into midfield to overload the centre — the prototype Pep FB.

full back.name: Achraf Hakimi-type rocket
full back.summary: Pure athletic engine — gets up and down the flank all day, threatens like a winger.

full back.name: Carvajal-type defensive FB
full back.summary: Defends first, supports second — the most decorated modern right-back.

full back.name: Pervis Estupiñán-type
full back.summary: Modern complete LB — attacks and defends with equal end product.

full back.name: Robertson-type engine
full back.summary: Pure aerobic monster — never stops running, delivers like a left winger.

full back.name: Kyle Walker-type pace
full back.summary: Recovery pace specialist — let him chase down anyone, the cover is automatic.

full back.name: Theo Hernández-type rocket
full back.summary: Marauding left-back with a rocket left foot — overlaps like a winger.

defensive midfielder.name: Rodri-type tempo controller
defensive midfielder.summary: The best #6 in the world — controls every game's tempo with elite scanning.

defensive midfielder.name: Casemiro-type destroyer
defensive midfielder.summary: Pure destroyer — wins the ball, kills attacks, lets others play.

defensive midfielder.name: Fabinho-type athletic shield
defensive midfielder.summary: Athletic shield — combines positional intelligence with raw athleticism.

defensive midfielder.name: Busquets-type positional
defensive midfielder.summary: Defends without running — reads the game faster than anyone alive.

defensive midfielder.name: Kovacic-type carrier
defensive midfielder.summary: Press-resistant carrier — escapes pressure with the dribble, finds the next pass.

defensive midfielder.name: Barella-type engine
defensive midfielder.summary: All-action engine — the modern Serie A midfield prototype.

defensive midfielder.name: Adam Wharton-type young #6
defensive midfielder.summary: Young English #6 who plays with the composure of a 30-year-old veteran.

defensive midfielder.name: Valverde-type box-to-box
defensive midfielder.summary: Hybrid #6/#8 — defends like a destroyer, finishes like a striker.

defensive midfielder.name: Bruno Guimarães-type
defensive midfielder.summary: Complete midfielder — combines Brazilian technique with European grit.

central midfielder.name: De Bruyne-type range passer
central midfielder.summary: Long-range passer who hurts defences from anywhere on the pitch.

central midfielder.name: Bellingham-type complete 8
central midfielder.summary: Generational midfielder — arrives in the box, defends, leads, scores.

central midfielder.name: Modric-type vision
central midfielder.summary: Sees what others miss — unlocks defences with one pass at 38 years old.

central midfielder.name: Pedri-type press-breaker
central midfielder.summary: Press-resistant micro-genius — escapes pressure to find the next forward pass.

central midfielder.name: Declan Rice-type engine
central midfielder.summary: Modern English engine — covers ground, wins duels, leads through energy.

central midfielder.name: Kroos-type metronome
central midfielder.summary: The German metronome — every pass perfectly weighted, the engine never breaks.

central midfielder.name: Sandro Tonali-type
central midfielder.summary: Italian composure with a 90-minute engine — controls tempo and defends.

central midfielder.name: Kobbie Mainoo-type
central midfielder.summary: Young academy prodigy with the composure of a senior midfielder.

central midfielder.name: Florian Wirtz-type
central midfielder.summary: Creative engine — beats his man and finds the killer ball in the same motion.

central midfielder.name: Fabián Ruiz-type
central midfielder.summary: Both-footed Spanish metronome — composes through pressure with elite range.

winger.name: Mbappé-type explosive
winger.summary: Pure vertical threat — pace and finish in the same player.

winger.name: Vinícius-type 1v1 dribbler
winger.summary: 1v1 specialist — isolates and beats his marker every single time.

winger.name: Salah-type cutting inside
winger.summary: Inverted winger — cuts inside and finishes like a striker.

winger.name: Bukayo Saka-type two-footed
winger.summary: Two-footed creator — equally dangerous either side, creates as much as he finishes.

winger.name: Jeremy Doku-type rocket
winger.summary: Lightning-quick winger — goes outside the FB and crosses with venom.

winger.name: Rafael Leão-type
winger.summary: Elegant long-strider — covers ground with effortless pace, dribbles through duels.

winger.name: Kvaratskhelia-type flair
winger.summary: Flair dribbler with end product — skill moves and finishes in equal measure.

winger.name: Olise-type creator winger
winger.summary: Playmaker from the wing — creates more chances than most #10s.

striker.name: Haaland-type penalty-box
striker.summary: Pure penalty-box predator — every chance finishes in the back of the net.

striker.name: Mbappé-as-9 explosive
striker.summary: Stretches teams by running in behind — pure pace forces deeper lines.

striker.name: Harry Kane-type deep-lying
striker.summary: Plays as a #9 + #10 hybrid — drops deep, links play, finishes chances.

striker.name: Lewandowski-type finisher
striker.summary: Pure technical executioner — finishes with whatever foot, from any angle.

striker.name: Lautaro Martínez-type
striker.summary: Relentless presser — leads the front-line press AND finishes chances.

striker.name: Alexander Isak-type
striker.summary: Elegant complete striker — both-footed, intelligent movement, clinical finish.

striker.name: Victor Osimhen-type
striker.summary: Athletic monster — beats defenders for pace, in the air, and on the ground.

striker.name: Ollie Watkins-type complete
striker.summary: Modern English #9 — elite movement, consistent finishing, all-action work rate.

striker.name: Nicolas Jackson-type
striker.summary: Marauding striker — endless runs in behind stretch defensive lines thin.

striker.name: Darwin Núñez-type chaos
striker.summary: Chaotic energy striker — high-xG misses but eventually everything goes in.
